entries.title: factoria docs read prints doubled carriage returns on Windows
entries.missing:
`factoria docs read <name>` on Windows writes every line ending as CR CR LF (
), so redirecting a doc to a file and extracting the recipe files from it (the menus doc is meant to be copied) yields files with a blank line after every line, and a text-mode reader sees two newlines. The menu recipe says 'copy the files as they are'.
entries.workaround:
Read the doc through `factoria call docs.read` (JSON) or normalise with a replace of 
 to 
 before extracting.
entries.suggestion:
Write the document to stdout in binary mode (or do not translate 
 to 
 twice) so only 
 or at most 
 appears.

entries.title: game.screenSize costs about 0.3 ms per read
entries.missing: Reading `game.screenSize` (or `.x`) from a script takes ~300 microseconds per read, 30 to 80 times more than every other call I measured (`entity.bounds()` 10 us, `world.find` 6 us, `entity.position.x` 14 us, `physics.raycast` 35 us). The template's follow_camera.js reads it twice per frame, so the camera alone was about 40% of the frame cost of a headless level (1200 frames: 3.1 s with it, 1.8 s without). It makes `factoria test` runs of long levels slow.
entries.workaround: scripts/follow_camera.js reads game.screenSize once and keeps the numbers.
entries.suggestion: Make game.screenSize a cheap property (cache the Vec2, or return a plain object); and have the 2d-platformer template's follow_camera.js cache it too.

entries.title: 2D kinematic platforms do not carry the bodies standing on them
entries.missing: A kinematic RigidBody2D that moves (a moving platform) does not take a body standing on it along: the guide and AGENTS.md say 'kinematic platforms carry the bodies on them' under 3D only, and the 2D recipes have no moving platform. In a headless test a player standing still on a platform that swings 96 px each way slid off it (offset changed by 90 px in 100 frames) with friction 0 and with friction 1, because player.js also sets velocity.x every frame.
entries.workaround: player.js casts a short ray under the feet, and when the hit entity has a kinematic RigidBody2D it adds that body's velocity.x to the player's own horizontal speed.
entries.suggestion: Carry dynamic 2D bodies that rest on a kinematic body (as 3D does), or expose the ground body (entity.groundBody / isGrounded() returning it) so a script can add its velocity without a raycast. Add a 2D moving-platform recipe to the AI guide.

entries.title: Menu recipe has no Spanish string table
entries.missing: docs menus says locales/es.json 'in the fixture has the same keys in Spanish', but the doc only prints locales/en.json. A game that wants two languages from the start (the recipe's own language switch) must translate the ~60 recipe strings itself and has no way to check they match the keys the recipe scripts use except by diffing against en.json.
entries.workaround: Wrote locales/es.json by hand from locales/en.json; tests/menus.test.js checks that both tables have exactly the same keys.
entries.suggestion: Ship the recipe's Spanish table in docs/MENUS.md (or as templates/menus/locales/es.json) and add `factoria new --menus` / a project.add_menus command that writes the whole recipe, so nobody copies 11 files out of Markdown.

entries.title: Test game object has no paused flag
entries.missing: In a test, `game.paused` (the natural thing to write after reading the pause recipe, where scripts use `game.paused`) is undefined, so `expect(game.paused).toBe(true)` fails with 'received undefined'. The scripting doc lists the test game members and none of them is the pause state; the working check is `time.scale` from the factoria module.
entries.suggestion: Add `paused` to the test game object (or say in docs scripting 'Tests' that the pause state is time.scale) and make reading an unknown member of the test game object throw with a did-you-mean instead of returning undefined.

entries.title: Shape2D is not shaded by Light2D
entries.missing: Only Sprite and Tilemap have `lit`; a Shape2D always draws at full brightness. A dark level lit by the player's lantern therefore cannot use Shape2D for hazards, enemies or platforms (the engine's own placeholder art), they would glow in the dark.
entries.workaround: Spikes and enemies are Sprites with small generated PNGs, platforms are solid-colour Sprites (no texture), all with lit true in the dark world. The player, embers and checkpoints stay Shape2D on purpose (they are light sources or must stay visible).
entries.suggestion: Add `lit` to Shape2D (same rule as Sprite.lit).

entries.title: scene.import_ascii warns about unused legend entries
entries.missing: Six levels share one legend (spikes, enemies, a moving platform...), but a level that does not use a glyph gets the warning "legend['m'] is not used in rows." (and the template's test asserts warnings equals []). There is no way to keep one shared legend file, or to silence the warning for a legend that is deliberately shared.
entries.workaround: The legend written into each levels/<id>.json holds only the glyphs that map uses.
entries.suggestion: Add `legendFrom: "levels/legend.json"` (a shared legend merged under the map's own) and do not warn about unused entries that come from it, or add `warnUnused: false`.

entries.title: No hook when an entity becomes active
entries.missing: The level end panel is spawned inactive and shown with `active = true`. Its Script's onStart runs only on the next step, so for one frame the panel shows the texts written in the prefab ('Time: 0:00.00') before the script writes the real ones. There is no onEnable/onActivate hook to fill a panel the moment it opens, and it is not obvious from the docs when onStart runs for an entity that is activated.
entries.workaround: level_end.js has an open(result, info) method that fills the texts at once; level.js calls it instead of relying on onStart.
entries.suggestion: Add onEnable()/onDisable() hooks (called when the entity becomes active or inactive, also for the first time), and state in docs scripting when onStart runs for inactive-then-activated entities.

entries.title: Long ASCII level maps are hard to author and edit by hand
entries.missing: Levels of 230 to 340 tiles wide (rows of that many characters, 23 rows) are tedious and error-prone to write directly in levels/<id>.json: one wrong count makes a ragged row, and moving a hazard means counting columns. scene.import_ascii only takes the finished grid, and the guide says not to write a level generator.
entries.workaround: Drew the maps with a throwaway script outside the project (a cursor that appends 'motifs' such as spikes, a pit with a checkpoint, a staircase, then writes the rows); the committed source of truth is still the ASCII in levels/<id>.json.
entries.suggestion: Let scene.import_ascii (or a new scene.ascii_edit command) take operations on an existing map: fill/replace a rectangle, insert or delete columns, place a glyph at (column, height above the ground), so an AI changes a map without rewriting every row; and report the column and row of every glyph in the result so it can be located again.

entries.title: platform catalog names and descriptions cannot be localized
entries.missing: factoria.json platform.achievements[].name/description and products[].title/description are plain strings with no localization key, so a store that shows them (Steam, Game Center, Play Games) shows English only, and the catalog is a second place with texts that a game with locales/*.json has to keep in sync by hand.
entries.workaround: The in-game screens ignore the catalog texts and read achievements.<id>.name / .description and shop.product.<id> from locales/*.json; the catalog keeps the English text for the store.
entries.suggestion: Let a catalog entry say name as a locale key or add a nameKey/descriptionKey, and have platform.achievements.list() and platform.purchases.products() return the translated text for the current language (or document that the catalog is for stores only).

entries.title: no way to test the none backend (no store) in a test
entries.missing: game.platform.set only offers signedIn and delayFrames. The case every exported game without a store plugin runs in (platform.has(...) false, every call rejecting unavailable) cannot be driven from a test, and it is the case the README of a game must promise to handle.
entries.workaround: Tests replace platform.has with () => false for the duration of a test (the scripts check has() before every call, so they take the no-store path) and restore it in a finally. The real rejections with code unavailable are not exercised.
entries.suggestion: game.platform.set({ backend: "none" }) that makes the fake behave as the none backend (has false, calls reject unavailable, signIn answers signed out) until reset().

entries.title: test runtime lacks Array.prototype.at, expect().toMatchObject and array methods on component colors
entries.missing: In a test, calls().at(-1) and expect(x).toMatchObject({...}) are not functions, and the value read from Shape2D.color / Light2D.color is array-like (Array.isArray is false, indices and length work) with no forEach, so color.forEach(...) throws not a function. The error says only TypeError: not a function, without naming which call.
entries.workaround: calls()[calls().length - 1], one expect(...).toBe per field, Array.from(color).
entries.suggestion: Ship ES2022 Array.prototype.at, add toMatchObject (the docs of factoria:test list the matchers), return real arrays for color fields, and name the missing method in the TypeError.

entries.title: a menu panel whose only autoFocus widget is not interactable has no focus for the pad
entries.missing: The menus recipe greys out buttons without a store (interactable false). When the autoFocus button of a panel (the shop pack) is one of them, nothing is focused when the panel opens and gamepad directions do nothing: the player is stuck. The rule text says autoFocus applies again only when a focused widget disappears.
entries.workaround: Left the buy buttons interactable without a store: a click answers with the same plain sentence as the status line.
entries.suggestion: Make the focus rule skip non-interactable autoFocus widgets and fall back to the first interactable one in reading order, or add the warning to the shop part of the menus recipe.

entries.title: world.emit from a test reaches listeners only at the next game.step
entries.missing: In a test, world.emit(name, data) followed at once by a check or by awaiting a script promise does nothing: listeners (world.on, Behaviour.on) are called at the next frame. platform.* answers are ready at once, so mixing the two is a trap: the first version of my store tests saw an empty fake store and no error.
entries.workaround: A settle() helper that does game.step(1) after emitting, then awaits the script, in every store test.
entries.suggestion: Say it in the scripting and testing docs next to world.emit, or deliver world.emit synchronously when called from a test.

entries.title: a store promise returned from a then callback is reported as an unhandled rejection
entries.missing: A best-effort chain written as `this.chain = this.chain.then(fn).catch(() => {})` where fn returns the promise of a platform call (for example `() => platform.achievements.unlock(id)`) logs `unhandled promise rejection ... failed: the player is not signed in` in a test when the store rejects, although the chain ends in a catch. Plain JS engines attach the handler one microtask later and report nothing.
entries.workaround: Wrap the call: `then(async () => { try { await fn(); } catch {} })`, so the store promise gets its handler at once.
entries.suggestion: Report an unhandled rejection only after the microtask queue drains (as Node does), or document that a platform promise needs its handler in the same turn.

entries.title: no onEnable/onDisable for a panel shown by active, and behaviour is null before its first activation
entries.missing: A menu panel placed inactive (prefab in the menu scene) gets no callbacks while hidden and its entity.behaviour is null until it is first shown, so a script cannot refresh itself each time the player opens it (the achievements list must ask the store again on every visit). onStart runs only the first time.
entries.workaround: The panel script has an opened() method; main_menu.js calls world.find(id).behaviour?.opened() after MenuStack.show, and onStart calls opened() itself for the first visit.
entries.suggestion: Add onEnable() / onDisable() to Behaviour, called when the entity (or an ancestor) becomes active or inactive, including the first time; or let MenuStack send a panel_shown event that hidden panels receive.
